title: Add delegated KMS witness and RBAC assertion revoker
author: Ayesha Qureshi
release_notes: Adds a delegated KMS witness path and an RBAC assertion revoker to reduce blast radius when operator claims are revoked; no customer-facing API changes.
description: Context: several customers required faster revocation and stronger non-repudiation for operator-issued KMS calls. This PR introduces a delegated KMS witness layer that records minimal provenance for each KMS operation and an RBAC assertion revoker component that enforces immediate denial for revoked operator claims. Summary: add a witness service that accepts signed KMS event proofs, extend audit headers with a compact proof token (proof_v1), add an in-memory revocation cache with eventual persistent snapshotting, update RBAC v2 decision pipeline to consult the revoker before allowing operator-scoped grants. Migration: deploy witness and revoker alongside existing audit-proxy in Canary; the witness accepts both existing and v1 headers and will backfill missing proofs for 24h. Safety: revoker defaults to shadow mode until the feature flag redwood.security.revocation.enabled is turned on for a tenant. Testing: unit + integration tests added, canary smoke run executed against Staging. Motivation: previously a revoked operator key could remain effective for several minutes due to cache TTLs and stale KMS delegations; this reduces that window to sub-second observed enforcement for most flows. Design notes: witness stores a compact hash (sha256) of the KMS call context, signed by the operator's ephemeral key; revoker stores revoked assertion fingerprints and immediately invalidates decision cache entries. Backwards compatibility: unchanged APIs for non-operator KMS consumers; tenants must opt-in to enforcement. See linked Linear tickets ENG-2021 and SEC-78.
commits_summary: initial: add witness service scaffold; impl: proof token format and signer; impl: revoker cache and eviction; api: audit header plumbing; tests: unit+integration for revoker and witness; ci: fix flake in auth test; docs: compliance guide; chore: bump deps for kms-client
changed_files_summary: pkg/kms/witness/service.go: added WitnessService with AcceptProof(ctx,proof) and background flusher; pkg/kms/witness/serializer.go: proof_v1 JSON compact serializer; pkg/auth/rbac/revoker.go: Revoker interface and in-memory implementation using a sharded map and LRU eviction; pkg/auth/rbac/middleware.go: decision pipeline hook consults Revoker before cache hit; services/audit/proxy/handler.go: attach compact proof token to outgoing audit envelope when available; deploy/helm/...kms-witness.yaml: new deployment and RBAC rules; docs/compliance/residency-proofing.md: new tenant opt-in guide; tests/integration/residency_witness_test.go: end-to-end happy-path and revocation enforcement; migration SQL: add revocations table and index.
review_comments: Jules Ortega: Can the witness handle replay attacks if an operator key is exposed? Response: witness stamps each proof with a monotonic nonce and tenant-scoped sequence; replay within a short window is deduplicated and recorded in metrics. Marta Li: How does this interact with region pinning? Response: proofs include region tag and the revoker enforces region-bound assertions, revocations are scoped per-geo; added tests for EU residence. Connor Hale: Please add a smoketest to the helm chart deployment. Response: added a post-deploy smokejob and updated chart values; approved after green CI.

notes_for_ops: Ops: enable feature flag redwood.security.revocation.enabled per-tenant to start enforcement; ensure DB migration scripts run before enabling; watch metrics witness.accepted_proofs and revoker.eviction.rate; rollback: disable feature flag and purge revoker in-memory cache if needed.
